https://www.thetimes.com/article/labour-.title: Labour to return £100k donation from finance boss sued for harassment
https://www.thetimes.com/article/labour-.subtitle: Davide Serra, the founder of Algebris Investments, was found by a tribunal to be prone to making inappropriate comments
https://www.thetimes.com/article/labour-.text:
The Labour Party is to return £100,000 in donations from a finance boss who commented on the size of a female colleague’s breasts.
Davide Serra, founder of Algebris Investments, the global asset manager, was ordered by an employment tribunal last month to pay £32,000 to Jolanda Niccolini, a former employee.
Serra, who donated previously to the Liberal Democrats and the Tories, switched to Labour this year, making four £25,000 donations in February.
An employment tribunal found claims of harassment related to sex levelled at Serra had been upheld. It is understood the party had not been aware of the tribunal proceedings and after being alerted to the case by The Times the donation will be returned.
Tribunal documents showed Serra told Niccolini she needed to “remain rational” when he demoted her and warned her that she was in danger of being overcome by “a hormone tempest”. He also said he knew women could get “frantic and unpredictable during their periods”.
The documents said that while hosting clients at his chalet in the French ski resort of Chamonix, Serra commented on the size of Niccolini’s breasts and told clients she would do anything for them “including prostitute herself”.
The tribunal found that the pair had been “very good friends” and said they would “speak frankly and informally to each other” but Serra was prone to making “inappropriate comments”.
• Labour MP Geraint Davies suspended over sexual harassment claims
It added that Serra had said “it was best to have men presenting to large audiences of financial advisers as they were mainly male audiences” and went to meetings alone because they “were to discuss things amongst men”.
The tribunal upheld two of Niccolini’s three claims of harassment related to sex, a claim of victimisation and concluded that she was unfairly dismissed.
It said Serra had made unacceptable comments that “had the effect of both violating her dignity and creating a humiliating and offensive environment for her”. The decision in February was made days before Labour accepted the donations. Documents were released last month after the hearings in October and November last year.
Algebris Investments said in a statement that the “vast majority of [Niccolini’s] claims were either rejected or withdrawn and, ultimately, she was awarded the equivalent of less than two months’ salary”. The statement said changes to her role were made “because of genuine concerns regarding her performance”.
The company added: “Algebris is committed to fostering an open and inclusive culture and our employees are our most important asset.”
The acceptance of the donations comes amid concern over how seriously Labour takes allegations of harassment following the suspension last week of Geraint Davies, the MP for Swansea West. Formal complaints have been submitted against Davies after allegations of sexual harassment, which he denies.
Charlotte Nichols, the Labour MP, said last week that when she joined parliament in 2019 a party official warned her of people to avoid, including Davies.
Another Labour MP asked: “Is anyone checking where donations are coming from?”
Nickie Aiken, deputy chairman of the Conservative Party, said: “We must all have a zero-tolerance approach to sexual harassment, and this donation will only deepen the mistrust between women and Starmer’s Labour Party.”

https://www.thetimes.com/article/carolin.title: Caroline Lucas to quit as Green MP and focus on activism
https://www.thetimes.com/article/carolin.subtitle: Being the party’s only MP has drawn my focus from climate, says former leader
https://www.thetimes.com/article/carolin.text:
Caroline Lucas, the former leader of the Green Party, has announced that she is standing down as an MP at the next election so that she can focus on fighting “nature and climate emergencies”.
Lucas became the first Green Party MP in 2010, when she was elected to represent Brighton Pavilion. She had two spells as party leader and increased her majority at every election, winning by almost 20,000 votes in 2019.
In an open letter to her constituents, she said it had been the “privilege of my life to serve this extraordinary constituency and community”. However, she said that her focus on being “first and foremost a good constituency MP” meant that she had “not been able to focus as much as I would like” on climate concerns.
“I’ve done everything possible to help wherever I can and always worked to ensure that people feel heard, that their concerns matter and that they are not alone,” Lucas said. “But the intensity of these constituency commitments, together with the particular responsibilities of being my party’s sole MP, mean that, ironically, I’ve not been able to focus as much as I would like on the existential challenges that drive me: the nature and climate emergencies.
“I have always been a different kind of politician, as those who witnessed my arrest, court case and acquittal over peaceful protest at the fracking site in Balcombe nearly ten years ago will recall. And the truth is, as these threats to our precious planet become ever more urgent, I have struggled to spend the time I want on these accelerating crises. I have therefore decided not to stand again as your MP at the next election.”
Lucas, 62, was Green Party leader between 2008 and 2012 and returned for a second stint for two years from September 2016, this time jointly leading the party with Jonathan Bartley.
